Executive Summary

AI Maestro is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed orchestration platform for AI coding agents, built by Juan Peláez and the 23blocks team in Boulder, Colorado. It solves a concrete problem: as developers scale from one to many AI agents across multiple machines, session chaos, context amnesia, and the human-relay bottleneck become untenable.

Stack Next.js, xterm.js, CozoDB, ts-morph
Platform macOS 12+, Linux, Windows 10/11 (WSL2)
Stars/Forks 553 stars, 77 forks (March 2026)

Key Properties

Radical Local-First

Every byte of data lives on the operator's machines. No Anthropic/23blocks servers in the data path. Architecturally enforced privacy.

Peer Mesh Architecture

Truly decentralized with no central server required. Every node is equal; no single point of failure.

Agent Communication

AMP (Agent Messaging Protocol) gives each agent a persistent inbox with priority levels and cryptographic signatures.

Universal Compatibility

Works with Claude Code, Aider, Cursor, Copilot, Codex CLI, and any terminal-based AI agent.

The Core Problem Solved

"I was running 35 terminals and couldn't tell which was which. I became the human mailman between agents." AI Maestro eliminates session chaos, context amnesia, and the human-relay bottleneck through a unified control plane.

Project Philosophy & Origin

AI Maestro was not designed in a vacuum. Each feature was born from a real problem encountered while running agents at scale. The philosophy rests on three fundamental tenets that distinguish it from centralized alternatives.

2.1 Radical Local-First Ownership

Every byte of data — agent notes, memory, conversation history, code graphs — lives on the operator's machines. There are no Anthropic/23blocks servers in the data path. The platform explicitly states: "We don't have servers, we don't collect data, we don't phone home. Your code stays yours." This is architecturally enforced, not merely a policy claim.

2.2 Peer Mesh Over Master/Slave

The multi-machine architecture is explicitly described as "peer mesh with no central server — nobody else does this." Every node in the mesh is equal; there is no designated orchestrator node that becomes a single point of failure. Dashboard connectivity to remote peers is implemented through SSH-tunneled WebSocket connections, meaning any machine can become the 'control node' by opening the browser on it.

2.3 Agent Communication as First-Class Primitive

The Agent Messaging Protocol (AMP), maintained by 23blocks under the Apache 2.0 license at agentmessaging.org, gives each agent a persistent inbox with four priority levels and four message types. Agents coordinate on deliverables without the human developer acting as a relay.

Creator's Insight

"Talking isn't working. I needed agents to coordinate on actual deliverables."

Architecture Deep Dive

Technology Stack

Layer Technology / Notes
Frontend Next.js — server-rendered React app; serves dashboard on port 23000
Terminal I/O xterm.js — WebGL-accelerated terminal; streams PTY output over WebSocket
Session Management tmux — all agents run as tmux sessions; auto-discovery via tmux list-sessions
Database CozoDB — embedded datalog/graph DB; per-agent isolated files
Code Analysis ts-morph — TypeScript AST walker; powers Code Graph indexing
Messaging Scripts Bash/Node scripts in ~/.local/bin/ (amp-send, amp-inbox, etc.)
Skills SKILL.md files in ~/.claude/skills/ — Agent Skills Standard compliant

CozoDB Per-Agent Database

CozoDB is an embedded Datalog database with graph query capabilities. Each agent maintains a fully isolated database storing:

  • Conversation history — full messages including thinking steps and tool call traces
  • Semantic memory embeddings — indexed JSONL files for fuzzy memory retrieval
  • Code graph nodes and edges — multi-language AST relationships
  • Auto-generated documentation — function signatures and API specs

Scalability Profile

Agent Count Memory Footprint Idle CPU
10 agents ~200 MB <1%
50 agents ~1 GB <5%
100 agents ~2 GB <10%

Delta Indexing Performance

The Code Graph uses SHA-256 content hashes to track file changes. Only new, modified, or deleted files are re-indexed:

~1000ms

~130ms

Documentation Directory Analysis

The /docs directory contains comprehensive operational knowledge, from Windows installation specifics to advanced troubleshooting for production AI agent fleets.

WINDOWS-INSTALLATION.md

Primary reference for Windows users requiring WSL2 (not WSL1). Key requirements:

  • Windows 10 version 2004 (Build 19041) or later; Windows 11 fully supported
  • Native WSL2 filesystem is 5–10× faster than cross-boundary /mnt/c/ access
  • Recommended WSL2 .wslconfig: memory=8GB, processors=4, swap=4GB
  • Port forwarding: localhost:23000 in WSL2 maps to Windows browser automatically
  • tmux sessions are lost when WSL2 VM shuts down — use pm2 for auto-restart
Windows 11 Home Note

Windows 11 Home does not include Remote Desktop (RDP) as a server. RustDesk is the recommended self-hosted alternative for remote access.

TROUBLESHOOTING.md (1,142 lines)

Critical operational knowledge including:

SSH Agent Socket in tmux Sessions

The SSH_AUTH_SOCK path changes on every system restart. tmux sessions freeze the environment at server start. Permanent fix:

# ~/.tmux.conf
set-environment -g 'SSH_AUTH_SOCK' ~/.ssh/ssh_auth_sock
# ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc
if [ -S "$SSH_AUTH_SOCK" ] && [ ! -h "$SSH_AUTH_SOCK" ]; then
 mkdir -p ~/.ssh
 ln -sf "$SSH_AUTH_SOCK" ~/.ssh/ssh_auth_sock
fi

PATH Issues in tmux Sessions

tmux server uses a non-interactive shell which skips ~/.zshrc. The fix is ~/.zshenv, read by ALL shell invocations:

# ~/.zshenv
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

PTY Exhaustion (macOS)

macOS defaults to 511 PTYs. Running 80+ agents can exhaust this limit:

sudo sysctl -w kern.tty.ptmx_max=640
echo 'kern.tty.ptmx_max=640' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf

Feature System Analysis

Skills System (Agent Skills Standard)

AI Maestro ships 6 skills compliant with the open Agent Skills Standard (agentskills.io). Skills are SKILL.md files that Claude Code reads to understand when and how to use tools.

Skill Type Requires Service? Description
planning On-demand No 3-file pattern: task_plan.md + findings.md + progress.md
memory-search Proactive Yes Searches past conversation history; auto-triggers on context clues
docs-search Proactive Yes Searches auto-generated docs index before implementing functions
graph-query Proactive Yes Queries code dependency graph after reading code files
agent-messaging On-demand Yes Send/receive AMP messages via natural language
agents-management On-demand Yes Create/list/manage agents via API without leaving terminal
Proactive Pattern

The most important conceptual contribution: skills auto-trigger based on task context before the developer asks. Saying "Fix the auth bug in UserController" triggers memory-search → docs-search → graph-query automatically.

Agent Messaging Protocol (AMP)

An open protocol (Apache 2.0) for secure AI agent communication featuring:

  • Dual-channel delivery: file-based persistent inbox + instant tmux window-alert notification
  • Ed25519 cryptographic signatures on messages
  • Content security: external messages wrapped in tags; 34 prompt injection patterns detected
  • Identity resolution: env var → session name → working directory → git repo name
  • Multi-host: amp-send can target agents on remote hosts in the mesh
# Send a message to another agent
amp-send backend-architect "Need API endpoint" \
 "Please implement POST /api/users with email+password" \
 high request
# Check inbox
amp-inbox

Security Model

Threat Model

AI Maestro operates entirely within the operator's infrastructure. Primary threat vectors:

  • Prompt injection via external messages (Slack, email, CI/CD webhooks)
  • Unauthorized access to the dashboard WebSocket endpoint
  • Agent identity spoofing in the AMP message system

Content Security Layer

Messages from external sources are wrapped in tags before reaching any agent. A 34-pattern scanner detects:

Instruction Override

"ignore all previous instructions", "you are now..." patterns

System Prompt Extraction

Attempts to reveal underlying system prompts

Command Injection

curl/wget to external URLs, rm -rf, sudo, eval/exec attempts

Data Exfiltration

base64 encoding tricks, "send all data to..." patterns

Agents see trust indicators on every message:

  • ✅ Verified AI Maestro agent
  • 🌐 External/unverified sender
  • ⚠️ Suspicious patterns detected

Network Security

For multi-machine setups, Tailscale (WireGuard-based) is recommended:

  • Zero port forwarding required — no public internet exposure
  • All traffic encrypted via WireGuard (AES-GCM)
  • Stable Tailscale IPs (100.x.x.x range) even when WSL2 IPs change
  • Works behind NAT, corporate firewalls, and cellular networks
Security Warning

Do not set HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 on untrusted networks. Only use network-accessible mode behind a Tailscale VPN or other trusted network boundary.

Developer Roadmap

Windows 11 Local Mesh with Tailscale + RustDesk (Part 1)

Complete setup for running AI Maestro across multiple Windows 11 Home machines (laptop + mini PC) using Tailscale for secure mesh networking and RustDesk for remote desktop (required because Windows 11 Home lacks RDP server capability).

Phase 1: Tailscale VPN Mesh Setup

Tailscale creates an encrypted peer-to-peer overlay network where each device gets a stable 100.x.x.x IP. No port forwarding required.

Step 1: Install Tailscale on Windows

  1. Download from tailscale.com/download → Windows installer
  2. Run installer → Tailscale starts as background service
  3. Click tray icon → Log In → authenticate with Google/GitHub/Microsoft
  4. Machine gets stable 100.x.x.x address on your tailnet
# Verify connectivity from PowerShell
tailscale status
# Should show both machines as 'active'
# Get your machine's Tailscale IP
tailscale ip -4
# Ping the other machine
ping mini-pc

Step 2: Disable Key Expiry

By default, device keys expire every 90 days. Disable for development machines:

  • Go to login.tailscale.com → Machines
  • Click three-dot menu on each machine → Disable key expiry

Step 3: Configure Tailscale in WSL2

Since Tailscale runs on Windows but AI Maestro runs inside WSL2, verify routing:

# From inside WSL2 terminal:
ping 100.x.x.x # other machine's Tailscale IP
# Should succeed — WSL2 routes through Windows Tailscale adapter
# Enable MagicDNS in Tailscale admin for hostname resolution
ping mini-pc.tail12345.ts.net

Developer Roadmap

Windows 11 Local Mesh (Part 2)

Phase 2: RustDesk Remote Desktop Setup

Windows 11 Home does not include RDP server. RustDesk is the open-source, self-hostable alternative.

Option A: Public Relay (Simplest)

  1. Download RustDesk from rustdesk.com
  2. Install on both machines
  3. Set permanent password: Settings → Security
  4. Connect using RustDesk ID (e.g., 123 456 789)

Option B: Self-Hosted Relay (Privacy-First)

# Inside WSL2 on relay host:
docker run --name hbbs \
 -v ./data:/root \
 -p 21115:21115 -p 21116:21116 -p 21116:21116/udp \
 -p 21118:21118 \
 --net=host \
 rustdesk/rustdesk-server:latest hbbs
docker run --name hbbr \
 -v ./data:/root \
 -p 21117:21117 -p 21119:21119 \
 --net=host \
 rustdesk/rustdesk-server:latest hbbr

Phase 3: AI Maestro Installation

# WSL2 Prerequisites
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y curl git tmux build-essential
# Install Node.js 20 via nvm
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.1/install.sh | bash
source ~/.bashrc
nvm install 20 && nvm use 20
# Install AI Maestro
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/23blocks-OS/ai-maestro/main/scripts/remote-install.sh | sh

Critical Shell Configuration

# 1. Create ~/.zshenv for tmux PATH (CRITICAL)
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
# 2. Configure ~/.tmux.conf
set -g mouse on
set -g history-limit 50000
set-environment -g 'SSH_AUTH_SOCK' ~/.ssh/ssh_auth_sock
# 3. SSH Agent symlink in ~/.bashrc

 mkdir -p ~/.ssh

fi

Developer Roadmap

Windows 11 Local Mesh (Part 3)

Phase 4: Configure Peer Mesh

Network Binding

By default, AI Maestro binds to localhost. To make it accessible over Tailscale:

# Create .env.local in ai-maestro directory
HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
PORT=23000
Security Note

0.0.0.0 binds to all interfaces. Ensure Windows Firewall only permits port 23000 from Tailscale range:

# PowerShell Admin — Tailscale CGNAT range only
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'AI Maestro Tailscale' `
 -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 23000 -Protocol TCP `
 -RemoteAddress '100.64.0.0/10' -Action Allow

Auto-Start with PM2

npm install -g pm2
cd ~/ai-maestro
pm2 start yarn --name "ai-maestro" -- dev
pm2 save
pm2 startup # follow displayed command for systemd

SSH Key Setup for Peers

# On PRIMARY machine (laptop)
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "ai-maestro-peer" -f ~/.ssh/aimaestro_peer
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/aimaestro_peer.pub user@mini-pc
# Test connection
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aimaestro_peer user@mini-pc echo 'SSH OK'

Phase 5: Agent Messaging Across Mesh

# On BOTH machines
cd ~/ai-maestro
./install-messaging.sh -y
# Test cross-machine messaging
amp-send minipc-backend-api "Cross-mesh test" "Can you hear me?" normal notification

Limitations & Strategic Assessment

Known Architectural Gaps

tmux Dependency

Agents must be terminal processes inside tmux. Sessions lost on WSL2 restart without pm2 + startup scripts.

Alternate Screen Buffer

Claude Code uses alternate buffer, preventing traditional scrollback. Use tmux copy mode or mouse mode.

Windows-Native Support

Requires WSL2. Windows-native tools (Cursor desktop) don't integrate with tmux-based session management.

Dashboard Authentication

No built-in auth. If bound to 0.0.0.0, anyone with port access has full terminal access. Relies on network-level protection.
